So if you get angry, everyone gets angry at the same time. If you are violent, everyone is violent at the same time. Do you want to live in a world like that? Obviously not. So that is what the categorical imperative is: act and do and think as though everything you do will be reflected throughout the universe and you are the universe itself.

Now, this idea has been misunderstood as the golden rule or do unto others as they would do unto you. But actually, it's a much higher concept. The higher concept is that imagine you are God yourself. Everything you do will be reflected throughout the universe. Then how would you behave? You would behave with the highest virtue because you want to make the world a better place. If you do bad things, people will do bad things to you.

The second idea is free will. Whatever you do cannot be coerced; it must come from your own desire, will, valition, and choice. Otherwise, it's wrong. I cannot make you do good; you only want to do good by yourself. If you want to do evil, you should do evil because it's your choice. Even though it leads to a worse world, maintaining the principle of free will is important.

The last idea is humans as the end. You have heard the phrase "the means to an end," right? A king might need to build a better world by starting wars and sacrificing a billion human beings. But Kant and Zoroaster would say that's wrong because every life, every human life, is as valuable as all human life together. You cannot sacrifice one person for the sake of others; that is fundamentally wrong.

These three things together give us the concept of Asha. It presents to us three new concepts that will revolutionize human history: the individual (what matters inside you), free choice, and truth. What is good for you, do it because you will it. The family, community, or nation's sayings do not matter; only what you feel in your heart does.

Zoroastrianism gives birth to three new religions: Judaism, Christianity, and Islam, which together affect billions of people on Earth. Zoroaster is the most important individual who ever lived because he creates the structure for montheism. He had a major impact on Greek philosophy, especially Plato's allegory of the cave.

Imagine we are in a cave; all prisoners chained to the ground, staring at shadows projected by a fire behind us. We call these shadows reality, but it is a shadow reality, all fake.
